main_body: A tall strip with a plain vertical wooden rail on the left. On the right are three stacked short posts, each with a small light square top (cross mark) over a brown front face, and grey stone brackets between them.
top_band: Left rail: none, it is a continuous vertical wood strip from row 0 down. The right posts have a light tan square about 4-5 rows tall (rows 2-6, 18-22, 34-38) with a darker cross mark.
evidence: The largest volume is the left wood rail, which runs about 48 rows as a flat front face with no top surface at all. The right posts have only a small square cap, with no distinct front-edge line and no eave shadow, and their faces are painted flat rather than inset. The grey bracket bits carry no readable top faces. The posts do not show the horizontal beams and base tops that a frame needs, so this reads as a front elevation with a small hat.

style.evidence: The wood has about 4 tones (light tan, mid brown, dark brown, near-black gap) with only a little grain. The left rail is long and nearly flat in value, and the dark gaps are large uniform fills. Compared with the stall and well references, which have 5-6 steps, per-tile highlights and rich texture, the tiles carry few colours and look thinner and flatter.
